title: Your dog is now your active companion in the end of the world
author: awezoomstudios
selftext:
We've spent the last week on something small that ended up meaning a lot to us. Shadow, the family dog, has always been part of «Still Breathing» — a mouth to feed, a brutal decision waiting to happen if your family gets hungry... But when you left the bunker to go scavenging, there was no visual feedback that he was by your side. It looked like if you walked into those ruined houses alone.

**Not anymore. Now Shadow comes with you.** He's there, at your feet — look down and you'll find him watching you. When you do, you can hear him breathe. Lean in and pet him and his tail goes, slow and happy; something in a dead, silent house that still wants to be glad you're there. Ask him and he sits. And sometimes he barks when he shouldn't, and your stomach drops, because out here noise is the thing that gets you killed.

We didn't add Shadow to make the runs easier. We added him because those houses are lonely, and a dog changes what loneliness feels like. My teenage son, who writes the story, was firm about one thing early on: Shadow has to matter. So now he does. He's an active companion. He can be hurt out there. He might not come home with you. And you'll feel it when it happens, because by then you've knelt in the dust and scratched his ears a hundred times.

I'm honestly not sure a breathing dog counts as a "feature". It doesn't move a number on a screen. But it's the part of the game we're proudest of this month. Here he is. Hope you like him.

If you want to follow along, or just come say hi, we're on Discord. [https://discord.gg/NFphS2j5Z9](https://discord.gg/NFphS2j5Z9)

comments.author: NebjWork
comments.body: Funny how I don't care that you used AI for the game but it feels awful to read "your" intentions through a LLM... Come on, make it really yours or at least change the sentence pattern to make it human. Maybe I'm the only one feeling like this though...

replies.author: awezoomstudios
replies.body: Shit, you're right. I had been working on it for the whole day and I was tired and I just wanted to post something before going to bed. Since I'm spanish I wrote a sketch and asked the AI to translate and enhance the language and didn't check it too much. Shame on me.

replies.author: NebjWork
replies.body: No problem mate, I hear you. It just too bad to work on a cool feature on a game for a week and to sell it cheap just because of some text!

replies.author: awezoomstudios
replies.body: Thanks for pointing it out, I rewrote it completely. I didn't even fix the possible grammar mistakes.

comments.author: Pristine_Good7326
comments.body: the aesthetics is stunning. also I like how the music matches so well with the surrounding

replies.author: awezoomstudios
replies.body:
We’ve been developing this game for almost a year. And I never worked so much on a single project in all my life. I’ve discarded thousands of assets, used all my knowledge in design and art to make it look great. I’ve composed music, expanded the soundtrack with AI to have lots of variations and better scoring, discarded thousands of variations… I’ve improved and enhanced the visual engine to the limit, and we have a lot of work still to do because in the game you can explore different locations and we’re putting a different story into each one. That’s supposing us hundreds of hours of development.

Unfortunately all I will get is AI slop comments everywhere. And it makes me terribly sad because I’m doing the best I can with the tools we have today. But I think you can use it the wrong way and just get any shit it throws at you or you can act as an art director and work as if you had a team working for you. 

Thanks for your comment. :)

replies.author: Pristine_Good7326
replies.body: Oh no! Please don't feel discouraged. After all haters just gonna hate. Let the work speak for itself. So far you're doing great! And it's easy for people to talk but not everyone can spend a year building a game.
